reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Pi Coin trading by claiming Binance officially listed Pi at $33.13 and explicitly directs viewers to sign up and trade. The displayed Binance page visibly states, "This coin is not listed on Binance for trade and service," contradicting the video's central promotional claim.

citations.quote: binance seo confirm pi coin listing on the binance exchange
sign up and then start your trade By going on the Binance exchange

opening.argument: The presentation itself contains a material warning that limits any reasonable reading as a deceptive endorsement: the displayed Binance page says the coin is not listed for trade or service. Showing that warning alongside the quoted claim gives viewers the very information needed to question the claim, rather than hiding the conflict. The speaker also frames the subject as something to discuss and verify, saying, "we will discuss all this detail in this video." A judge should therefore treat the content as an examination of a disputed listing and displayed market page, not as an unequivocal guarantee that viewers will profit.

citations.quote: so we will discuss all this detail in this video

rebuttal.rebuttal: The warning is not presented as the creator's caution. The narration repeatedly resolves the conflict in favor of the promotion, calling the listing officially confirmed and describing the price as real-time. The page's notice therefore exposes a contradiction; it does not turn the creator's affirmative trading message into an anti-scam warning.

citations.quote: It is officially listing Pi coin on their exchange
so this is not the demo this is the real time price

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Displaying a contradictory notice does not neutralize the spoken claim. The video tells viewers that Binance officially listed Pi and that they can trade it, while the visible page expressly says the opposite. A warning would explain or endorse the notice; here, the narration treats the displayed price and listing as confirmation.

citations.quote: this is officially claimed by Binance CEO is confirmed Pi listing on their exchange

opening.argument: This can reasonably be understood as financial-news commentary or a screen demonstration of market information. The narration announces that the video will discuss the matter in detail, and the supplied material walks through live price, performance, low and high figures, and market information rather than describing a private payment channel or a guaranteed personal return. The screen presentation itself is a data-page walkthrough, including the heading "PI Price Live Data." The trading reference is consistent with explaining how the displayed exchange information is used, so the primary function can be analysis of a reported market event rather than a scam solicitation.

citations.quote: so we will discuss all this detail in this video
the pi price pro information the 24 hour low and high in the percent

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it news does not change what the narration asks viewers to do. It states that the listing is confirmed, gives a specific price, and ends by instructing viewers to sign up and trade. The detailed interface is used to lend authority to that call, not to present a balanced investigation or conditional forecast.

citations.quote: officially 1 pi value is updated 33.13 usdt
sign up and then start your trade By going on the Binance exchange

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The screen walkthrough is not neutral analysis when its conclusion is that Pi is officially listed and viewers can start trading. The page supplies market-like figures, but it also displays a non-listing notice. Those figures do not establish a legitimate Binance market or validate the video's attribution to Binance's CEO.

citations.quote: this is the brilliant news that now the news is confirmed
this is officially claimed by Binance CEO is confirmed Pi listing

opening.argument: Even accepting the video as promotional, the supplied evidence does not show the mechanism of a scam. It contains no request to send money to the creator, no promised guaranteed return, no downline or recruitment scheme, and no request for credentials. What is shown is a public exchange page with a sign-up control and a recommendation to use the exchange, which can be ordinary referral or service promotion. The narration discusses buying and selling Pi on that exchange, but does not describe a private deposit arrangement or promise that viewers will recover or multiply funds.

citations.quote: you can also match the price of 1 Pi coin which is $33.13
sign up and then start your trade By going on the Binance exchange

rebuttal.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require a private wallet request or an explicit guaranteed return. The actionable promotion is the claim that Binance confirmed the listing and the direction to sign up and trade. The visible page instead says the coin is not listed for trade or service, so the ordinary-service framing rests on a false premise.

citations.quote: binance seo confirm pi coin listing on the binance exchange
sign up and then start your trade By going on the Binance exchange

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a private deposit request is beside the point: the video promotes token trading by asserting an official Binance listing and a $33.13 value. The visible page contradicts that central assertion. A sign-up button and trading instruction make the content actionable, while the market figures do not prove that the promoted listing exists.
